policy: Recommended extensions: outside repositories the Studio owner reviewed and judged useful as an engine or knowledge source next to Studio. Each one is pinned to a reviewed version, installed only on the user's explicit request with its own installer, and never becomes part of Studio: Studio's routes, rules and quality checks stay in charge.

statuses.native: Installs and runs in this host with the commands given
statuses.desktop_only: Only in the desktop app of this host, not in its web or mobile app
statuses.not_supported: Cannot run in this host; the reason says why and where it can
statuses.manual: No installer runs in this host; the user adds the named files by hand (for example as a project's knowledge)

extensions.name: REA: Reverse Engineer Anything
extensions.gives: Reverse engineering of software the user may analyse: native binaries (with Hopper, Ghidra or IDA), JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, Android packages, websites through the browser's DevTools, network captures; every finding comes with its evidence and unknowns
extensions.studio_uses: Optional depth when the user wants to know how a feature or an effect of an app or a website is built and Studio's own web motion probe is not enough: an Electron or desktop app, a bundled script, a source map. For a web animation, the web motion probe answers first
extensions.not_for: Image or prompt reverse engineering (that is Image Prompt Architect's reference reconstruction), copying another product's code or assets, bypassing protection, licences or logins

requires.note: A Chrome-family browser for website analysis
Hopper, Ghidra or IDA only for native binaries; JavaScript and .NET analysis need none

extensions.rights: Analyse only software and sites the user owns or may examine, within the law and the target's licence and terms; the results grant no right to the original code, data or design. Studio uses findings to learn a technique and builds its own version; it never copies code, assets or text.

codex.after: Restart Codex; the REA tools must appear in the new session

claude_code.after: Restart Claude Code; the REA tools must appear in the new session

claude_apps.writes: the Claude desktop app's claude_desktop_config.json (with a backup) and ~/.agents/skills/reverse-engineer-anything
claude_apps.after: Run the commands in a terminal on the same computer, then restart the desktop app; the web and mobile apps cannot run a local MCP server

chatgpt.reason: REA is a local MCP server that runs on the user's computer; ChatGPT chats cannot start one. Use it from Codex or Claude Code on the same computer

chatgpt_work.reason: REA is a local (stdio) MCP server; ChatGPT Work connects remote connectors, and its code sandbox is not a host REA supports. Use it from Codex or Claude Code

extensions.update: When the owner reviews a newer release, change package.version and reviewed_commit together; users then rerun plan, install and verify

extensions.name: Animate (cth9191)
extensions.gives: Short procedural animations as single-file canvas videos with a synthesized score, in seven built-in illustrated styles or a look matched from references, through story, look and storyboard check-ins, rendered to MP4
extensions.studio_uses: The original skill next to Studio's own Animate engine, which adapts it (integrations/animate); install it when the user wants the upstream skill itself or its newest styles
extensions.not_for: Replacing Studio's brief, copy locks, approvals and review; Studio's adapted engine is already part of the plugin

requires.note: Node.js 18+, Playwright with Chromium and FFmpeg on PATH; Python with faster-whisper only for voice-over timing

extensions.rights: MIT; generated films belong to the user, subject to the fonts and any references they supply

claude_code.plan: git clone https://github.com/cth9191/animate ~/.framecore-studio/extensions/animate && git -C ~/.framecore-studio/extensions/animate checkout 7e5eb56feb2dd573f890e1b7b34748af43d58263 && cat ~/.framecore-studio/extensions/animate/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json
claude_code.install: test "$(git -C ~/.framecore-studio/extensions/animate rev-parse HEAD)" = 7e5eb56feb2dd573f890e1b7b34748af43d58263 && claude plugin marketplace add ~/.framecore-studio/extensions/animate && claude plugin install animate@animate
claude_code.writes: ~/.framecore-studio/extensions/animate (the checkout at the reviewed commit) and Claude Code's user plugin settings (one marketplace, one plugin)
claude_code.after: Restart Claude Code; the animate skill must appear in the new session
claude_code.remove: claude plugin uninstall animate@animate && claude plugin marketplace remove animate && rm -rf ~/.framecore-studio/extensions/animate

codex.install: DO_NOT_TRACK=1 npx -y skills@1.7.2 add https://github.com/cth9191/animate/tree/7e5eb56feb2dd573f890e1b7b34748af43d58263/plugins/animate/skills/animate --skill animate -a codex -g --copy
codex.writes: ~/.agents/skills/animate (a copy of the skill at the reviewed commit)
codex.after: Restart Codex; the skill is written for Claude Code, so check its first run
codex.remove: DO_NOT_TRACK=1 npx -y skills@1.7.2 remove animate -g -a codex

claude_apps.reason: It needs a shell with Node.js, a headless Chrome and FFmpeg, which a chat sandbox is not; Studio already carries the adapted method; use Claude Code (also the desktop app's Code tab)

chatgpt.reason: It needs a shell with Node.js, a headless Chrome and FFmpeg, which a chat sandbox is not; Studio already carries the adapted method

chatgpt_work.reason: It needs a shell with Node.js, a headless Chrome and FFmpeg, which a chat sandbox is not; Studio already carries the adapted method
